package_info.package_manager: cdn (JavaScript library, distributed via web CDN)
package_info.package_versions: All versions served from cdn.polyfill.io since February 2024
package_info.why_malicious: The CDN at polyfill.io, after being acquired by a new owner, began serving JavaScript payloads that inject malware into mobile devices of users visiting any website embedding the polyfill.io CDN. The injected code is designed to evade detection and can execute arbitrary malicious actions on client browsers, violating the trust model of third-party JavaScript CDNs.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code loads and executes JavaScript from cdn.polyfill.io, which may inject additional malicious scripts into the page, perform device fingerprinting, redirect users, or exfiltrate sensitive data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The CDN, previously trusted, is now under new ownership and is serving JavaScript that injects malware into client browsers. The code is dynamically generated and can change at any time, making it difficult to audit or detect.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior is to serve only polyfill code for browser compatibility. Instead, the CDN is serving code that performs malicious actions such as data exfiltration, redirection, or further script injection.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be to serve only polyfill code for browser compatibility, without any dynamic or third-party script injection.
key_indicators: Dynamic JavaScript payloads from a previously trusted CDN
Code changes after domain ownership transfer
Suppression of user complaints and issue reports

attack_chain.action: Website includes a script tag referencing cdn.polyfill.io.
attack_chain.leads_to: Browser loads and executes JavaScript from the CDN.

attack_chain.action: CDN serves JavaScript payload that may include malicious code (e.g., malware injection, data exfiltration, redirects).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes in the context of the user's browser.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code performs actions such as device fingerprinting, credential theft, redirection, or further script injection.
attack_chain.leads_to: User device is compromised or user data is exfiltrated.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected or dynamic JavaScript payloads from cdn.polyfill.io
Script tags referencing cdn.polyfill.io in web application source
JavaScript code that injects additional scripts or performs network requests to untrusted domains at runtime
file_indicators: References to cdn.polyfill.io or polyfill.io in HTML, JavaScript, or package code
network_indicators: Subsequent network requests from browser to attacker-controlled domains after loading polyfill.io
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan web application source code and dependencies for references to cdn.polyfill.io or polyfill.io. Monitor runtime JavaScript execution for dynamic script injection, unexpected network requests, or DOM modifications originating from polyfill.io scripts. Use web application firewalls or browser security tools to block or alert on third-party scripts from untrusted or recently transferred domains. Implement Subresource Integrity (SRI) checks to prevent execution of tampered CDN scripts.
